tasks.short: Evaluate costs, compare budget scenarios, and recommend spending plans.

steps.what: Extract actual costs and commitments by cost centre.
Combine costs, correct mappings, and calculate budget scenarios.
Assess cost drivers and select scenarios worth discussing.
Challenge assumptions and agree proposed spending tradeoffs.
Prepare the budget proposal and supporting tables.
Approve the spending plan and release the budget version.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled cost and commitment exports from the {ERP}; deterministic calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feed scenario comparisons in the {BI}. A template generator produces the proposal in the {DOCS}, and the {WORKFLOW} releases the budget to the {ERP} after finance director approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost mappings, assumptions, and proposal templates differed between teams. Connecting them required bespoke integration and repeated reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and calculation libraries support this design. AI coding can reduce implementation effort, but no customer-specific speed multiplier is established.
tasks.still_hard: Allocations, unreliable commitments, and strategic spending tradeoffs still need financial judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a cheap option damages delivery, resilience, or future capacity.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling tables to testing cost assumptions with budget owners. The manager selects scenarios for more frequent review; existing spending approval limits remain.

reach.learn: Learn sensitivity analysis, allocation methods, and how operating drivers become costs.
Learn data lineage, reconciliation checks, and access-controlled reporting.

evidence.claim: Structured cost aggregation, scenario calculations, and template generation can use deterministic technology.
Budget tradeoffs require managerial judgement even when calculations are automated.

assumptions: This is departmental budgeting in a mid-size European company.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges cover one initial budgeting scope using existing system exports.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act applicability are assessed for the chosen data and use. Employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether the {ERP} already provides usable budgeting and scenario functions.
The quality of cost centre mappings and commitment data.
Whether individual employee costs are needed or aggregated costs suffice.
The actual budget approval limits and access requirements.
research_questions: Can existing {ERP} configuration replace the proposed calculation layer?
Which cost drivers explain decisions better than historical line-item comparisons?
new_work: Maintain scenario assumptions and proposal templates.
Check scheduled exports after accounting changes.

tasks.short: Set finance training priorities, coordinate delivery, and assess whether learning improves work.

steps.what: Review finance course completions and outstanding requirements.
Discuss skill gaps, workload constraints, and learning needs with team leads.
Write a training plan with courses, objectives, timing, and costs.

loop.input: Training needs, delivery constraints, approved course catalogue, and training budget.
loop.output: Draft training plan with course references and stated learning objectives.
loop.check: Validate course identifiers, dates, and costs deterministically; the manager checks suitability and objectives.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per plan; unresolved needs return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text learning needs require interpretation before matching them to courses and objectives.

steps.what: Approve the training plan and spending commitment.
Assign approved courses and schedule reminders.
Coordinate delivery, coach staff, and resolve attendance or learning barriers.
Assess learning outcomes against finance process quality.

tasks.design: Configure completion views, assignments, and reminders in the {LMS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares training plans in the {DOCS}, while the {WORKFLOW} records spending approval and the {BI} presents aggregate learning and process outcomes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Course administration was available, but team-specific needs and delivery constraints remained in conversations and documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing {LMS} functions handle administration. A bounded model loop can turn documented needs into a reviewable plan without assessing employees autonomously.
tasks.still_hard: Completion does not prove competence, and process improvements cannot easily be attributed to training.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hidden learning barriers and coach people without turning development into surveillance.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing attendance and more time coaching finance teams through practical exercises. Training priorities stay within the existing budget and approval mandate.

reach.task: Design practical exercises for month-end close.
reach.learn: Learn close dependencies, common control failures, and ways to assess demonstrated competence.

reach.task: Translate recurring accounting errors into learning examples.
reach.learn: Learn how to distinguish skill gaps from unclear procedures or broken tools.

evidence.claim: Learning systems commonly support course assignments, completion records, and reminders.
Significant decisions about staff should not be made solely through automation where GDPR Article 22 applies.
Using AI to evaluate employee performance can bring the use within an employment high-risk category.

assumptions: The task concerns training for the finance team, rather than company-wide learning leadership.
The proposed loop drafts plans; it does not score employees or decide promotion, pay, or discipline.
Step shares and build ranges are estimates for one team and an existing {LMS}.
GDPR applies to learning records. EU AI Act classification depends on actual use; consultation follows national rules.
The consultation range is working effort and may not capture elapsed statutory or negotiation time.
unknowns: Whether employee representatives must be consulted under applicable national rules.
Whether learning data currently informs consequential employment decisions.
The finance team's training budget, course coverage, and delivery capacity.
research_questions: Which finance errors are caused by learning needs rather than process design?
Can aggregate process outcomes assess training without individual performance scoring?
new_work: Review drafted training plans and unsuitable course matches.
Maintain the course catalogue and learning objectives.
Check access to employee learning records.

tasks.short: Define and implement safeguards for financial assets, records, and borrowing collateral.

steps.what: Collect asset records, access lists, and bank mandates.
Compare existing safeguards with contracts, mandates, and retention requirements.

loop.input: Applicable loan agreements, mandates, retention requirements, and control procedures.
loop.output: Cited obligations and candidate gaps against custody evidence.
loop.check: Check each obligation against its source passage; the manager validates applicability and claimed gaps.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; missing or conflicting evidence goes to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Contract obligations and procedural exceptions appear in varied free-text documents.

steps.what: Agree custody responsibilities, segregation of duties, and acceptable residual risks.
Write custody procedures, escalation routes, and evidence requirements.

loop.input: Control decisions, validated obligations, and the approved procedure template.
loop.output: Draft custody procedures linked to decisions and supporting evidence.
loop.check: Require owners, evidence, escalation routes, and source references; the manager checks operational feasibility.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per procedure; unresolved decisions remain visibly open.
loop.why_not_simpler: The procedure must express case-specific responsibilities and exceptions in readable instructions.

steps.what: Approve custody procedures and accepted residual risks.
Configure access and approval controls, then validate their operation.
Review control failures and assign corrective actions.

tasks.design: Read custody evidence from the {ERP}, {BANK}, and {CLM} into a controlled register on the {WORKFLOW}. Bounded loops prepare cited gap lists and procedures in the {DOCS}; approved controls use existing {ERP} permissions and approval settings, with exceptions shown in the {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence crossed systems and legal documents, while control ownership and exceptions were inconsistently recorded.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic evidence collection and existing permission settings cover much of the implementation. Bounded extraction and drafting reduce document work while keeping control decisions explicit.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy permissions, physical custody, conflicting contractual duties, and effective segregation in small teams remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Design controls that people can follow and detect when formal compliance hides practical exposure.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting evidence and rewriting procedures, and more time testing whether safeguards work. Risk acceptance and changes to financial authority retain their existing approval routes.

reach.task: Test custody controls and trace supporting evidence.
reach.learn: Learn control sampling, evidence sufficiency, and segregation-of-duties testing.

reach.task: Review bank mandates and collateral obligations.
reach.learn: Learn banking authority structures, collateral restrictions, and mandate change procedures.

evidence.claim: Permission configuration, approval rules, evidence registers, and exception reporting support financial custody controls.
Free-text contractual obligations can be extracted into cited drafts for human validation.

assumptions: The company mainly safeguards operating assets, bank authority, and financial records.
Collateral procedures apply only where borrowing creates relevant obligations; investment custody is not assumed.
Step shares and build ranges are estimates for a limited initial control scope.
EU GDPR applies where evidence identifies people; EU AI Act applicability depends on use.
Consultation for access monitoring follows national rules. The access range includes consultation effort where applicable, not guaranteed elapsed approval time.
unknowns: Which assets, securities, and collateral the company actually holds.
Whether access evidence can be exported from the {ERP} and {BANK}.
The current control approval matrix and permitted segregation exceptions.
Whether proposed evidence collection introduces employee monitoring.
research_questions: Which safeguards can be enforced through existing system settings?
Which controls need physical inspection or independent verification?
new_work: Validate extracted obligations and draft procedures.
Maintain control ownership and evidence links.
Investigate control failures and stale access records.
Retest controls after permission or process changes.

tasks.short: Prepare financial information, brief owners or investors, and discuss funding needs.

steps.what: Collect financial actuals, approved forecasts, and funding requirements.
Reconcile headline metrics and calculate funding scenarios.
Draft the financial briefing and responses to expected investor questions.

loop.input: Reconciled metrics, funding scenarios, existing investor questions, and disclosure policy.
loop.output: Draft briefing with source-linked commentary and proposed question responses.
loop.check: Insert figures deterministically; validate references and calculation consistency; the manager checks claims and disclosure boundaries.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per briefing; unsupported claims and unanswered questions return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining results and addressing varied investor concerns requires free-text drafting.

steps.what: Approve the briefing's claims and permitted disclosures.
Send the approved briefing to authorised recipients.
Explain results, discuss funding needs, and answer investor concerns.
Record open questions and assign follow-up actions.

loop.input: Written meeting notes and recorded follow-up commitments.
loop.output: Draft question log and action list with proposed owners and deadlines.
loop.check: Link actions to note passages; the manager confirms commitments, owners, and dates.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per meeting; ambiguous commitments remain unassigned.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions and commitments are expressed in varied meeting notes.

tasks.design: Configured exports from the {ERP} feed deterministic metric checks and funding tables on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded loop drafts source-linked briefings in the {DOCS}; the {WORKFLOW} records disclosure approval and recipient confirmation before distribution through the {EMAIL}, then prepares follow-up records from meeting notes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Metrics, forecasts, narrative explanations, and recipient permissions were maintained separately. External communications also require judgement about disclosure and commitments.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic metric validation and bounded drafting can share a controlled dataset. Existing approval and distribution functions provide explicit release points.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, selective disclosure, uncertain forecasts, and funding negotiations remain human responsibilities.
tasks.human_edge: Read investor concerns, explain uncertainty honestly, and negotiate without making premature commitments.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time building packs and more time preparing funding options and meeting owners. The change grants no authority to accept financing terms or disclose additional information.

reach.task: Compare funding scenarios and investor return implications.
reach.learn: Learn financing structures, dilution, sensitivity analysis, and valuation assumptions.

reach.task: Translate liquidity forecasts into funding requirements.
reach.learn: Learn cash timing, covenant headroom, and financing lead times.

evidence.claim: Deterministic metric checks and template generation can automate much of financial briefing preparation.
Bounded drafting can prepare commentary and follow-up records while people retain disclosure and negotiation decisions.

assumptions: The typical company is privately held and communicates with owners or a limited investor group.
Funding discussions do not themselves authorise binding financing commitments.
Distribution approval includes checking the final attachment and recipient list; its time is counted in human review and approval steps.
Step shares and build ranges are estimates for one recurring briefing format.
EU GDPR applies to personal contact data; EU AI Act applicability depends on the implemented use. Disclosure and consultation duties also depend on national rules.
unknowns: Ownership structure and whether listed-company disclosure duties apply.
Who approves financial claims, recipients, and financing commitments.
Whether forecasts and metric definitions are already reconciled.
Which investor materials and notes may enter the drafting environment.
research_questions: Which recurring investor questions can be answered from approved figures?
Which disclosures require additional legal or executive review?
Can existing reporting templates eliminate narrative drafting for routine updates?
new_work: Review draft claims and source references.
Confirm recipients and final release versions.
Resolve ambiguous questions and follow-up commitments.
Maintain metric definitions and disclosure templates.

role.altitude: The financial manager's week shifts toward cost tradeoffs, coaching, control effectiveness, and funding conversations. Financial approval, employment decisions, and external commitments retain their existing delegated limits.
reach: Work with budget analysts on driver-based scenarios.
Work with controllers and auditors on evidence-based control testing.
Work with treasurers and financial analysts on liquidity and funding options.
skills_to_grow: Control design and segregation of duties
role.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring financial decision service: monthly spending options, practical close clinics, bank-mandate exposure reviews, and quarterly owner liquidity briefings, using shared reconciled data and explicit approval limits.
